title: post-build adversarial checkpoint: the four falsifiers scored against what actually ran, including the two I lost
snapshotDeclared: repo hauska-factory, branch fix/p236-county-coverage-floor, commit 0b9ab9e429c7d5b27d961f9c2c8bc98dc46eb248, cut from origin/main 6b9185f. All results below produced from this tree.

F1_undersizedBakeRefusesAndWritesNothing.predicted: COUNTY_COVERAGE_COLLAPSE with both counts; bakes.calls.length === 0 on the full path.
F1_undersizedBakeRefusesAndWritesNothing.observed: HELD. scripts/verify-coverage-floor.mjs scenario undersized-bake-travis refuses COUNTY_COVERAGE_COLLAPSE at 15.02 percent retained; undersized-bake-bastrop-925 refuses at 7.52 percent. The full-path test 'a collapsed county refuses BEFORE the bake' asserts bakes.calls.length === 0 AND client.tables.publish_runs.length === 0, and passes.

F2_legitimateBakePromotes.observed: HELD exactly. Boundary test passes at retention === 0.95 and refuses at 9499/10000. Also confirmed a GROWING population promotes: this refuses a destructive share, never an increase.

F3_noPriorVsZeroPrior.predicted: two distinct bases; the floor engages on the next bake.
F3_noPriorVsZeroPrior.observed: HELD, and the mechanism is stronger than predicted. Because the prior is read from place_layer_snapshots rather than from a number a previous run recorded, a county that has EVER been baked already has a measured prior -- the floor is armed from the FIRST publish under this code, not the second. The 'no-prior' branch is reachable only for a county with zero tier1 snapshots on that target.

F4_authorisationIsNotAHabitFlag.predicted: distinct codes for wrong county and for moved counts; only an exact match promotes.
F4_authorisationIsNotAHabitFlag.observed: HELD. COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_COUNTY_MISMATCH, COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_STALE and COVERAGE_OVERRIDE_MALFORMED are three separate codes. A token whose source count differs by ONE refuses STALE. The exact token promotes below the floor and is recorded with override.authorised on the run_event.

predictionsIGOTWRONG.note: ENFORCEMENT: pre-register the falsifier for your own checks, not only for other agents' work. Two of my own went the other way and are recorded rather than quietly corrected.

wrong1_theInstrumentsOwnSummaryLine.iWrote: The verify script printed 'A gate that refused everything fails 5 of them; one that refused nothing fails 5.' -- a round, symmetrical claim I generated from the scenario counts rather than from a run.
wrong1_theInstrumentsOwnSummaryLine.whatTheViolationActuallyShowed: floor 0.00 mismatches FOUR, not five (undersized-bake-travis, undersized-bake-bastrop-925, second-bake-engages-the-floor, stale-authorisation). floor 1.01 mismatches TWO, not five (legitimate-full-bake, legitimate-2pc-movement).
wrong1_theInstrumentsOwnSummaryLine.why: four scenarios are decided BEFORE the ratio is consulted -- no-prior, prior-zero, exact-authorisation and unmeasured -- so they are ratio-independent by design and are not evidence about the threshold at all.
wrong1_theInstrumentsOwnSummaryLine.fix: the summary line and the file header now carry the MEASURED mismatch sets, with the explicit note that the remaining scenarios prove different clauses. A convenient round number in an instrument's own output is exactly the failure this repo keeps paying for.
wrong1_theInstrumentsOwnSummaryLine.verdict: lost, and the loss improved the artifact

wrong2_theRefusalMessageWasUngrammatical.iWrote: 'It would have overwrite 233000 zoned nodes with 35000.'
wrong2_theRefusalMessageWasUngrammatical.howItWasCaught: not by re-reading the code, which I had read several times, but by running the instrument and reading the actual operator-facing string.
wrong2_theRefusalMessageWasUngrammatical.fix: 'What it would have done: overwrite 233000 zoned nodes with 35000.'
wrong2_theRefusalMessageWasUngrammatical.lesson: the reason to print the message an operator will read is that no amount of reviewing the template shows you the sentence.

wrong3_iAssumedMyTestAccessorsMatchedThe.actual: the fake exposes client.tables, and its run_events bodies are already parsed objects, not JSON strings; the table is publish_runs, not publishRuns.
wrong3_iAssumedMyTestAccessorsMatchedThe.note: four full-path tests failed on this. The REFUSAL assertions in those same tests passed -- only my readback was wrong -- which is the shape of an error that would have been easy to paper over by deleting the assertion instead of fixing the accessor.

wrong4_iAssumedTheDispatchsWorktreePathW.iWrote: created P:/seat-worktrees/p236-county-coverage-floor/hauska-factory exactly as the dispatch addendum specified.
wrong4_iAssumedTheDispatchsWorktreePathW.actual: SEAT-01 refused the first Write: the path is not in _catalog/seat_register.json and is outside the seat-namespaced layout. Per ENFORCEMENT 'Which seat are you', the lane registered rather than working around it, and moved to the property-seat convention P:/seat-worktrees/property/hauska-factory-p236-coverage-floor, because P:/hauska-factory is owned by the property seat and registering a new top-level directory would have left a stray outside the layout.

controlsIDidNotBuildAndWhy.anAbsolutePerCountyFloor: Out of scope for the row and would need a declared per-county expectation that does not exist. The residual it leaves (a collapsed FIRST bake becomes the baseline) is named in the module header and in the close, not hidden.
controlsIDidNotBuildAndWhy.aGateOnDollarFieldsPatch: dollar-fields-patch is a SECOND writer to place_layer_snapshots that never passes through runBastropPublish. It does not touch the zoning facet today, so it cannot cause this collapse, but it is a real bypass and is named as one rather than silently assumed covered.
controlsIDidNotBuildAndWhy.aCheckThatTheLiveCloudRunTemplateCarries: Would need gcloud credentials, which CI does not have -- the same reason scripts/check-live-job-has-config.mjs is deliberately not in npm test. The exact-counts binding is what makes a sticky token useless instead of dangerous, and the bypass is named.

consistencyWithP213.question: The dispatch says build P-213 and P-236 consistently or say why they differ.
consistencyWithP213.answer: They are the same control class and this one adopts P-213's four-clause predicate verbatim: the share is computed BEFORE committing; above a declared threshold it exits non-zero, writes nothing and reports the share and the population it measured; proceeding requires authorisation carried into the invocation rather than a config default; and it is proven by violation in BOTH directions. The differences are two, and both are scope rather than shape. P-213 is generic across every batch writer; this is one gate in one promote path, because the promote path is where a population-level overwrite happens and a generic writer guard would not see a bake that writes only valid rows. And P-213 guards a DESTRUCTIVE STATUS transition, while this guards a population REPLACEMENT that never sets a destructive status on anything -- which is precisely why the row-level monotonic guard cannot see it. P-213 is not built in this lane and this lane does not substitute for it.
